meta.generatedFrom: TypeScript (the parity contract — never regenerate from Rust)
meta.description: price = max(0.01, fairValue × exp(clamp(s, ±MISPRICING_CAP))), across a spread of fair values including zero, subnormal, negative and non-finite.
notes: Math.exp IS A PARITY RISK. It is the only transcendental in the mispricing hot path and its argument is bounded to [-0.9, 0.9], so a shared correctly-rounded exp over that narrow range is a realistic fix if Rust disagrees.
Math.max(0.01, NaN) is NaN in JS. Rust f64::max(0.01, NaN) returns 0.01. This differs and the port must special-case it, or guarantee its inputs are never NaN.
Negative fair values survive the multiply but are then floored to 0.01, so applyMispricing never returns a negative price — except for NaN.
meta.floatEncoding: bits = raw IEEE-754 f64, big-endian, 16 uppercase hex digits. dec = shortest round-trip decimal, informational only.
meta.nanPolicy: Every NaN is recorded as 7FF8000000000000 (the pattern of Rust f64::NAN). V8 does not emit a stable NaN sign/payload, so only NaN-ness is contractual — compare NaN results with is_nan(), not with bits.
